title: Rigor in Context
creator: Beth Kullberg
subject: College Admissions
description: See why course rigor is judged against what your high school offers: compare the share of available advanced courses taken, not the raw count.

learningObjectives: Students will compare course schedules across high schools with different offerings and differentiate between the number of advanced courses a student took and the rigor that number represents.

controls: Advanced courses taken slider (0 to offered)
Elena, Jordan, and Emily preset buttons

keyQuestions: Is a student penalized for attending a school with few advanced courses? Why not?
What does this model leave out that a real counselor would consider?
Why does Jordan's counselor rate Jordan higher than the model does?
commonMisconceptions: Students at small schools are at a disadvantage because they can't take many APs.
assessmentOpportunities: Students explain, using the share of available courses taken, why two students with the same number of AP courses receive different rigor ratings.
